title: 4,000-year-old skeletons suggest ancient Egyptian princesses were skilled in using bows and weapons
description: New research reveals ancient Egyptian princesses' bones show signs of weapon handling. Skeletal marks indicate repeated archery and weapon use, challenging symbolic interpretations. Princess Ita's bones suggest strong grip strength, while Itaweret's show bow drawing adaptations. Princess Noub-Hotep's remains and burial arrows strongly support active weapon engagement. This evidence broadens understanding of elite women's activities in Middle Kingdom Egypt.
